content: Voriconazole interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to changes in drug levels and effects. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Voriconazole and Cyclosporine: Voriconazole increases cyclosporine levels by altering its metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and cyclosporine therapy should be adjusted as needed. 2. Voriconazole and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases voriconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 3. Voriconazole and Danazol: Danazol increases voriconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 4. Voriconazole and Dapsone: Voriconazole increases dapsone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Voriconazole and Daridorexant: Voriconazole increases daridorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 6. Voriconazole and Darifenacin: Voriconazole increases darifenacin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Voriconazole and Darunavir: Voriconazole increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 8. Voriconazole and Dasatinib: Voriconazole increases dasatinib levels and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Voriconazole and Deflazacort: Both drugs decrease serum potassium, and voriconazole increases deflazacort levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce deflazacort dose to one-third if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Voriconazole and Degarelix: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Voriconazole and Desflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Voriconazole and Desipramine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 13. Voriconazole and Deutetrabenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Deutetrabenazine does not clinically prolong the QT interval at maximum recommended doses, but certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 14. Voriconazole and Dexamethasone: Voriconazole increases dexamethasone levels, while dexamethasone decreases voriconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Voriconazole and Dexlansoprazole: Voriconazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Voriconazole and Diazepam: Voriconazole increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. 17. Voriconazole and Dichlorphenamide: Both drugs decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Voriconazole and Diclofenac: Voriconazole increases diclofenac levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Do not exceed a diclofenac dose of 50 mg BID. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Voriconazole and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Voriconazole increases levels of these drugs by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 20. Voriconazole and Dihydroergotamine: Voriconazole increases dihydroergotamine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Voriconazole and Diltiazem: Voriconazole increases diltiazem levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Voriconazole and Disopyramide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 23. Voriconazole and Disulfiram: Disulfiram increases voriconazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 24. Voriconazole and Docetaxel: Voriconazole increases docetaxel levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 25. Voriconazole and Dofetilide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Voriconazole and Dolasetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Voriconazole and Donepezil: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Voriconazole also increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 28. Voriconazole and Doravirine: Voriconazole increases doravirine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 29. Voriconazole and Doxepin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Voriconazole and Doxorubicin: Voriconazole increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Voriconazole and Dronabinol: Voriconazole increases dronabinol levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Voriconazole and Dronedarone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Voriconazole and Droperidol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Voriconazole and Dutasteride: Voriconazole increases dutasteride levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 35. Voriconazole and Duvelisib: Voriconazole increases duvelisib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce duvelisib dose to 15 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 36. Voriconazole and Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated at efavirenz doses of 400 mg/day or higher. 37. Voriconazole and Elacestrant: Voriconazole increases elacestrant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Voriconazole and Elagolix: Voriconazole increases elagolix levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 39. Voriconazole and Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Voriconazole increases levels of these drugs by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Voriconazole and Eletiptan: Voriconazole increases eletiptan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Voriconazole and Eliglustat: Voriconazole increases eliglustat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Voriconazole and Eluxadoline: Voriconazole increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Voriconazole and Elvitegravir: Voriconazole increases elvitegravir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Voriconazole and Encorafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Voriconazole and Enfortumab Vedotin: Voriconazole increases enfortumab vedotin toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Voriconazole and Entrectinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Voriconazole and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases voriconazole levels, while voriconazole increases enzalutamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Voriconazole and Epinephrine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
